recognize_zh: 大型腫瘤細胞核呈淡藍、細胞本身完全不染 PD-1，只有少數小型背景 T 細胞呈棕色膜狀陽性，可作為內部陽性對照；代表漿母細胞淋巴瘤腫瘤細胞 PD-1 陰性。
features: Sheet of medium-to-large tumor cells with round-to-oval vesicular nuclei
Tumor cells are negative for PD-1
Scattered small lymphocytes with membranous/granular PD-1 positivity (internal positive control)
Positive cells are sparse and not arranged in rosettes around tumor cells
Faint background cytoplasmic blush without specific staining
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for PD-1 shows a diffuse population of medium-to-large tumor cells with vesicular nuclei that are negative for PD-1. Only scattered small reactive lymphocytes show membranous to granular PD-1 staining, serving as an internal positive control, and they do not form rosettes around the neoplastic cells. The neoplastic cells therefore do not express PD-1, which argues against a T-follicular helper phenotype and is consistent with the plasmablastic lymphoma immunoprofile.

ddx.dx: Nodal T-follicular helper cell lymphoma, angioimmunoblastic type
ddx.vs: Neoplastic cells are PD-1+/CD10+/CXCL13+ T cells with expanded FDC meshworks, whereas here PD-1 highlights only scattered background cells.
PD-1+ T cells form rosettes around scattered large B cells, a pattern not seen here.
Also PD-1-negative, so PD-1 does not help; separation relies on clinical, EBER and marrow findings.
